# Nutrient classifier model card: nutrient_run1.keras

## Purpose
Classifies an accepted leaf photo as no deficiency or one of four nutrient deficiencies, with a confidence, as one input to fusion. In user-facing messages a nitrogen call is worded "possible nitrogen deficiency".

## Ship status
Verdict: SHIPS under the rule fixed before training (`docs/nutrient_ship_rule.md`; source `results/nutrient_run1/nutrient_run1_test/test_decision.json`). This means the rule passed on this dataset. It does not mean deficiency detection works in the field (see Known failure modes).

- Version: nutrient-v1
- File: nutrient_run1.keras (33436273 bytes)

- Weights are not in git. Location: MyDrive/maize-project/models/nutrient_head/run1/nutrient_run1.keras
- TensorFlow 2.21.0. Input: 224x224 RGB, preprocessing "efficientnet".
- Classes, in model output order: nitrogen, no_deficiency, phosphorus, potassium, zinc.

## Data
Raw images in `data/raw/nutrient_deficiency/Nutrition_dataset`, mapped to classes by `scripts/resplit_nutrient_data.py`. The dataset's provenance and licence are not recorded in this repository. The first split leaked near-duplicate images between train and test (`results/nutrient/leakage_check.txt`) and was replaced by a split by independent photo group (`scripts/split_nutrient_grouped.py`, 65/15/20, seed 42; manifest `results/nutrient/split_v2_manifest.csv`). ## Training
Source: `models/nutrient_head/run1/training_run.json`, `scripts/train_image_classifier.py` in Colab. EfficientNetB0 with ImageNet weights, two phases: head only (learning rate 0.001), then the last 40 base layers unfrozen with BatchNormalization kept frozen (learning rate 1e-05). Epochs run: phase 1 8, phase 2 12. Batch size 32, seed 42, balanced class weights, TensorFlow 2.21.0. Best validation accuracy 0.9672 (the checkpoint was chosen on validation, so validation figures are optimistic). One training run only (decisions in `docs/nutrient_run1_decision.md`).

## The pre-registered ship rule (`docs/nutrient_ship_rule.md`; values from `test_decision.json`)
| Rule | Cutoff | Measured on test | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Macro recall | at least 0.70 | 0.9527 | True |
| 2. Lowest class recall | at least 0.50 | potassium 0.8653 | True |
| 3. no_deficiency recall | at least 0.80 | 0.9918 | True |
| 4. Predictions at confidence 0.80 or more | at least 100 images from at least 20 photos, precision at least 0.85 | 2555 images from 451 photos, precision 0.9656 | True |

Healthy images predicted as a deficiency at confidence 0.60 or more (the level at which fusion flags): 0.0021. The test set holds 2773 images from 460 independent photos. The cutoffs are judgment calls fixed before training, not derived values.

## Thresholds and fusion settings
- Confidence bands (shared with disease, from the RAP fusion rules): strong at 0.8 or more, weak from 0.6, uncertain below.
- Cap: nitrogen counts as weak whatever its confidence. Status: post-hoc decision after the test evaluation (docs/nutrient_posthoc_findings.md); kept through submission whatever the phone photos show, because a small smoke test can reveal failures but cannot prove nitrogen detection works.
- Calibration applied: False (temperature 1.0).

## Known failure modes
- Potassium is confused with phosphorus (63 images) and zinc (55); zinc is confused with phosphorus (14) and potassium (21). Potassium has few independent test photos, so its recall is uncertain. The intervals in the table above show how uncertain these figures are; potassium has the fewest independent test photos (33)..
- **Nitrogen is captured differently from every other class.** Nitrogen images are large camera photos and the other classes are tiny crops, so its near-perfect score is not evidence that nitrogen deficiency can be detected. The capture-style check:

```text
=== nitrogen: 1535 images ===
  filename styles: {'IMG camera name': 1535}
  top image sizes (width x height): ['1200x686 (4)', '1200x556 (4)', '683x1200 (4)']
  distinct sizes: 1320, median file size: 150.3 KB
=== no_deficiency: 2430 images ===
  filename styles: {'NNNN_a variant': 2430}
  top image sizes (width x height): ['100x200 (1458)', '200x100 (972)']
  distinct sizes: 2, median file size: 8.3 KB
=== phosphorus: 2970 images ===
  filename styles: {'NNNN_a variant': 2970}
  top image sizes (width x height): ['100x200 (1782)', '200x100 (1188)']
  distinct sizes: 2, median file size: 8.2 KB
=== potassium: 4301 images ===
  filename styles: {'NNNN_a_b tile': 4300, 'other': 1}
  top image sizes (width x height): ['200x100 (2236)', '100x200 (2065)']
  distinct sizes: 2, median file size: 5.2 KB
=== zinc: 2545 images ===
  filename styles: {'NNNN_a variant': 2545}
  top image sizes (width x height): ['100x200 (1527)', '200x100 (1018)']
  distinct sizes: 2, median file size: 8.3 KB
```

  A diagnostic on the validation split only (nitrogen images cropped, shrunk to 100x200 and recompressed to match the other classes) gave nitrogen recall 1.0000 before and 0.9827 after, on 231 images (errors: 3 called zinc, 1 called phosphorus). That is little evidence of reliance on resolution or file size. It is not proof, since every image is resized to 224x224 before the model sees it and colour, background and lighting were not changed. Potassium, also separable by file size and tiling, was not tested.

## Limitations
- Every class is studio-style. No field test was run (the phone-photo test was not run, `docs/limitations.md`), so performance on phone photos is unknown and likely lower.
- The leakage check shows no group in two splits and no cross-split pair at phash distance 5 or less (`tests/test_nutrient_split.py`). It uses the same distance as the grouping, so it is a consistency check. A rotated copy of a photo would not be caught.
